questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P. of pictographic and phonetic symbols, provided

Q. invaluable insights into their culture, religion,

R. ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, a complex system

S. and daily life for over three millennia
questions.solution_en:
The sentence begins most logically with part R, "Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, a complex system," which introduces the main subject "Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs" and provides an appositive phrase "a complex system" to describe it.

Part P, "of pictographic and phonetic symbols, provided," directly follows R, further elaborating on what kind of "complex system" it is ("of pictographic and phonetic symbols") and then introducing the main verb "provided."

Next, part Q, "invaluable insights into their culture, religion," serves as the object of the verb "provided" from part P. It details what the hieroglyphs provided - "invaluable insights" - and begins to list the areas of these insights.

Finally, part S, "and daily life for over three millennia," completes the list of areas ("culture, religion, and daily life") into which insights were provided and adds the duration for which this was true ("for over three millennia").

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is RPQS.

The complete sentence after rearrangement is: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, a complex system of pictographic and phonetic symbols, provided invaluable insights into their culture, religion, and daily life for over three millennia.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

My elder brother said, "I must learn driving rules."
options_en: My elder brother said that he had to learn driving rules.
My elder brother said that he must be learning driving rules.
My elder brother said that he should be learning driving rules.
My elder brother said that he would learn driving rules.
questions.solution_en:
When "must" denotes morality or universality, there isn't any change in the use of "must".

For example:

The Professor said, "We must love our country."

The Professor said that we must love our country.

However, if the use of "must" doesn't denote universality or morality, then the tense form changes as per the normal rules.

For example:

Rahul said, "I must go to school at once."

Rahul said that he had to go to school at once.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· Inverted commas ("...") are replaced with 'that'.

· In the given sentence 'must' doesn't denote universality or morality. So, 'must' will change to 'had to'.

· The pronoun 'I' changes to 'he'.

None of the options except (a) follows these rules. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: My elder brother said that he had to learn driving rules.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

The introduction of African cheetahs to India was planned without considering their spatial ecology, according to researchers who warn that the released animals may come into conflict with people in the neighbouring villages. Spatial ecology addresses the fundamental effects of space on the movement of individual species and on the stability of multispecies communities. A total of 20 cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa were introduced to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh last year to establish a free-ranging population - for the first time since their extinction in India 70 years ago. Scientists of the Cheetah Research Project of Leibniz-IZW in Namibia argue that in southern Africa, cheetahs live in a stable socio-spatial system with widely spread territories and densities of less than one individual per 100 square kilometres (km²). The plan for cheetahs in Kuno National Park assumes that the high prey density will sustain high cheetah densities, even though there is no evidence for that, they said. In a letter published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice on Thursday, researchers noted that as Kuno National Park is small, it is likely that the released animals will move far beyond the park's boundaries and cause conflicts with neighbouring villages.

According to a calculation of the local prey density, it was calculated that 21 adult cheetahs could be sustained by the prey base in Kuno National Park - equivalent to a density of about three individuals per 100 km². Based on their research results from a long-term study of the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in Namibia, as well as comparable work in East Africa, scientists from the Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Leibniz-IZW warn against overestimating the carrying capacity of the area. The carrying capacity is usually between 0.2 and 1 adult per 100 km² for cheetahs under natural conditions. This is true not only for Namibia but also for the ecologically very different conditions in the Serengeti ecosystem in East Africa which has a much higher density of prey, they said. The team formulated predictions about the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in their new habitat, identifying controversial issues and hidden core assumptions of the reintroduction plan. These assumptions ignore important aspects of the cheetah socio-spatial system.

What is spatial ecology according to the passage?
options_en: It is the study of a species in a particular ecosystem and how it behaves around other species.
It is the study of multispecies communities and the stability of the species in an ecosystem.
It is the study of the movement of a species inside a space and the sustainability of other species in the space.
It is the study of the movement of a species with respect to its surroundings and the movements and eating habits of the species in the system.
questions.solution_en:
The first paragraph states that "Spatial ecology addresses the fundamental effects of space on the movement of individual species and on the stability of multispecies communities." According to this, the statement in option (c) is the most appropriate definition.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

How you choose to conduct _____ private life is your own business!
questions.solution_en:
The possessive pronouns ('yours' and 'ours' in the given statement) are generally not followed by the noun. So, these options are negated.

Here, a possessive adjective/determiner would fit. The apt possessive determiner to denote the subject 'you' is 'your' ['our' is used for 'we'].

The complete sentence is: How you choose to conduct your private life is your own business!

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Note: Possessive Pronouns: The pronouns mine, yours, hers, his, ours, and theirs are known as possessive pronouns: they refer to something owned by the speaker or by someone or something previously mentioned. For example: The pen is mine.

Possessive Determiners/Adjectives: Words like 'my', 'our', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', and 'their' are known as possessive adjectives (or possessive determiners). They come before nouns and indicate ownership of the noun. Example: "The teacher asked the students to open their drawing books."

In an increasingly noisy and overstimulated world, a new travel trend called silence tourism is emerging, where people seek destinations that promise stillness, solitude, and an escape from digital distractions. Unlike traditional vacations focused on entertainment or sightseeing, silence tourism encourages introspection and emotional detox. Remote monasteries in Bhutan, soundproof forest cabins in Finland, and silent retreats in the Himalayas are gaining popularity among urban dwellers looking to reset mentally. This form of travel doesn't merely offer peace - it fosters a deep reconnection with one's thoughts, often leading to improved well-being. Travellers are deliberately disconnecting from smartphones and social media, choosing instead to listen to nature or their own inner voices. In a time when constant connectivity is equated with productivity, silence tourism challenges that belief by promoting mindfulness and calm as equally valuable. It turns travel into a meditative experience, revealing that silence, often overlooked, is a luxury many didn't realize they needed.

Which of the following is the best antonym for the word "overlooked" as used in the passage?
questions.solution_en:
The word "overlooked" in the passage means something that has been neglected, not noticed, or given little attention.

Option (a) "Ignored" means deliberately paying no attention to something. This word is similar in meaning to "overlooked," not the opposite, so it cannot be the correct antonym.

Option (b) "Alleged" means something that is claimed without proof. This word has no direct connection to the idea of noticing or neglecting something, making it irrelevant in this context.

Option (c) "Recognized" means acknowledged or noticed, especially in terms of importance or value. This is the best antonym for "overlooked" because recognizing something is the opposite of ignoring or failing to notice it.

Option (d) "Abandoned" means something that has been given up completely or left behind. While it shares a negative tone with "overlooked," it implies intentional desertion rather than unintentional neglect or lack of awareness. It is not the appropriate antonym of the given word.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

"Oh, Mary, please don't be moody, not today. I told Harry all about how polite and intelligent and cheerful you are," she said. She'd met him at a business meeting when her company bought the company Harry worked for, and since then she'd been driving over the border to Canada every weekend to see him, leaving me at Dad's. Don't get me wrong, I loved staying with Dad, but I missed my Mom-weekends. We used to make popcorn and watch late-night TV, then sleep in and eat cold breakfast cereal together. Now, when she came to pick me up on Sunday afternoons, she always looked glowing and energetic - and much happier than she ever looked after a weekend spent with me. Last Monday she said something about her and Harry getting married, and that this trip might be the time when he pops the question. The only obstacle before him was meeting me. "I'll be sugar and spice and everything nice, I promise," I said sarcastically, staring out at the Canadian countryside. It pretty much resembled the American countryside only . . . it was more Canadian, somehow. Bigger and emptier, just as I imagined Harry; bigger than Dad, with an enormous head with lots of empty space inside.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that converts the given sentence into the superlative degree.

The river Ganga has some of the purer water on earth.
options_en: The river Ganga has some of the most purest water on earth.
The river Ganga has some of the very purest water on earth.
The river Ganga has some of the more purest water on earth.
The river Ganga has some of the purest water on earth.
questions.solution_en:
The original sentence uses "purer," which is the comparative degree of the adjective "pure." To convert it to the superlative degree, "purer" becomes "purest," indicating the highest degree of purity. Option 4 correctly uses "purest" without redundant modifiers like "most" or "very," which are unnecessary since "purest" is already the superlative form. The phrase "some of the purest" indicates that the Ganga's water is among the purest, which aligns with the original meaning. The other options either use incorrect grammar or redundant modifiers.

Option 1: The river Ganga has some of the most purest water on earth. Using "most" with "purest" is grammatically incorrect, as "purest" is already the superlative form. This creates a double superlative, which is redundant.

Option 2: The river Ganga has some of the very purest water on earth. "Very" is an intensifier that can be used with positive adjectives (e.g., "very pure"), but with superlatives like "purest," it is unnecessary and stylistically awkward in formal English.

Option 3: The river Ganga has some of the more purest water on earth. "More" is used for comparative forms (e.g., "purer"), not superlatives. Combining "more" with "purest" is grammatically incorrect.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Jennie asked me, "Why are you doing this to me?"
options_en: Jennie said to me why I was doing that to her.
Jennie told me why was I doing that to her.
Jennie asked me why I am doing that to her.
Jennie asked me why I was doing that to her.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

For example:

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

'Asked' is already present in the direct speech.

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Present Continuous tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Past Continuous tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The verb 'are doing' (present continuous) is changed into 'was doing' (past continuous).

· The pronouns 'you' and 'me' are changed into 'I' and 'her' respectively.

· 'This' is changed to 'that'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Jennie asked me why I was doing that to her.

Hence, the answer is option d).
